title: hud: dynamic panels — board proxy, digest, peers (stub-tested)
description: Per design doc §Dynamic layer. Extend ~/hud/_hud/server.mjs + ui: GET /api/dyn/board proxies hud.config.json sources.board.url, on success caches to _hud/generated/board.json; upstream down -> serve snapshot with stale:true + its generated_at; no snapshot -> 503 JSON (never a crash/500 stack). GET /api/dyn/digest shells sources.digest.cmd (lectio digest), same cache/fallback contract; lectio absent -> 503, server stays alive. Peers: on server start and POST /api/refresh/peers, read peers/*.md frontmatter (gh:, repos:), run `gh search prs --author <gh> --state open --json number,title,repository,updatedAt` per handle, write _hud/generated/peers.json; gh absent -> keep last snapshot. UI: needs-you dial (count of state=="needs_you"), MY PRS, PEERS IN FLIGHT, RECENT ACTIVITY panels; each greys out with snapshot timestamp or hides when no data. Tests in _hud/test/dynamic.test.mjs, HERMETIC: stub upstream via node http server on ephemeral port; stub gh via PATH shim script; required named cases: proxy-success-writes-snapshot; upstream-down-serves-stale-snapshot; no-snapshot-503-not-crash; peers-json-from-fixture-frontmatter-and-shimmed-gh; missing-lectio-503-server-alive. Still zero npm dependencies. Commit ~/hud with [bead-id].

comments.text:
Dynamic layer shipped: `~/hud` commit 8de0df2 `[agents-00b88a] feat(hud): dynamic panels — board proxy, digest, peers` (3 files, +1404/-40: `_hud/server.mjs`, `_hud/ui/index.html`, `_hud/test/dynamic.test.mjs`). Still node stdlib only — no npm, no node_modules.

## What was built

**One degradation ladder, shared by every proxied source** (`serveSource` in server.mjs): live → `200 {stale:false, cached_at, data}` and the snapshot is written; upstream broken → `200 {stale:true, cached_at, data, error}` from `_hud/generated/<name>.json`; no snapshot → `503 {source, error, cached_at:null}`. Snapshots are `{cached_at, data}` with `data` holding the upstream payload verbatim, written tmp+rename so a reader never sees a half-written file. A failed cache write is logged and swallowed — losing the cache must not lose the live response.

- `GET /api/dyn/board` — proxies `sources.board.url`. Non-2xx, non-JSON, oversized (>2 MB) and timeout (4 s) all count as failure, so an upstream login page or a 500 body is never cached as if it were a board.
- `GET /api/dyn/digest` — runs `sources.digest.cmd` via execFile (no shell; the command string is tokenized into argv, so `cli; rm -rf /` is inert argv, not two commands), 8 s timeout, 4 MB stdout cap.
- Peers — `readPeerHandles()` reads `peers/*.md` frontmatter (`gh:`, falling back to the filename), then one `gh search prs --author <h> --state open --json number,title,repository,updatedAt,url` per handle, sequentially (bounded load on a shared rate limit), max 32 peers / 20 PRs each. Writes `generated/peers.json` as `{generated_at, peers:[{handle, prs:[...]}]}`. Refresh runs at server start *after* listen and off the request path, and on `POST /api/refresh/peers`; concurrent refreshes collapse onto one in-flight promise so the ⟳ button can't fan out into a `gh` storm. `GET /api/dyn/peers` is snapshot-only and never shells out, so opening the HUD cannot stall on `gh`.
- Two deliberate degradation rules: **all** handles failing (no `gh`, no auth) leaves the previous snapshot byte-identical rather than overwriting it with an empty one; a *partial* failure writes the fresh snapshot and reports the per-peer `error`. Handles that aren't login-shaped (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}$/`) are skipped rather than passed to a subprocess.
- **UI** — header dial counts `state == "needs_you"` (green live / amber from-snapshot / `—` unavailable); MY PRS, PEERS IN FLIGHT (handle · N open · latest `updatedAt` as relative time · PR links), RECENT ACTIVITY. Three panel states per the spec: live, greyed+dashed with `as of <time>`, or `hidden` when the route 503s. Every row is a link out (`http(s)` only, else inert text) — no action buttons anywhere, per the watch-only invariant. One ⟳ re-fetches tree+board+digest and POSTs `/api/refresh/peers`.
- Config is the only switchboard: `hud.config.json` read per request (edit without restart), and a source absent from `sources` returns 503 even when a stale snapshot exists — absent source ⇒ absent panel. No URL, handle, or project name in code; fixtures use `peer-a`/`owner/repo-one`/`example.invalid`.

## Tests — `node --test _hud/test/` : 41 pass, 0 fail (289 ms)

14 new in `_hud/test/dynamic.test.mjs`, all hermetic (tmp `HUD_ROOT`, stub upstream = `node:http` on port 0, stub `gh` = shim script on a per-test PATH that logs its argv, stub digest = script written into the fixture). Required five, exact names, all green: `proxy success writes snapshot` · `upstream down serves stale snapshot` · `no snapshot yields 503 not crash` · `peers json from fixture frontmatter and shimmed gh` · `missing lectio yields 503 server alive`. Plus: digest cached-then-replayed-when-broken, wrapped-observations unwrapping, unconfigured source, upstream 500/non-JSON, no-`gh` keeps snapshot, no-snapshot peers 503, method/route rejection, command tokenizing, implausible-handle rejection. Asserts are on specific values — exact `gh` argv per handle (`search prs --author peer-a --state open --json number,title,repository,updatedAt,url`), exact peer records, `cached_at` identity between response and snapshot file, snapshot bytes unchanged after a failed refresh, and "GET peers invoked gh zero times".

The 16 pre-existing static tests stay green untouched. A sibling agent's `sessions-lib.test.mjs` (11 tests, bead agents-0b4975) landed in the same directory mid-run and passes alongside; its `_hud/sessions.mjs` is still an unwired library, so nothing of mine collides with it.

## Live check — no upstreams running, `HUD_PORT=8124 node server.mjs`

```
board:  503  {"source":"board","stale":true,"cached_at":null,"error":"fetch failed"}
digest: 200  stale=false, array len 10   (generated/digest.json written)
peers:  200
tree=200 index=200 board2=503     PROCESS ALIVE
log: hud: /Users/jamesgardner/hud | hud: http://127.0.0.1:8124/ | hud: peers refreshed
```
Never a 500, never a raw stack (asserted in tests too), server alive after every failure path.

## Deviations, stated

1. **Response envelope.** The brief said "return upstream JSON"; the route returns `{source, stale, cached_at, data}` with the upstream JSON verbatim under `data`. Spreading `stale`/`cached_at` into an unknown upstream schema risks colliding with its own keys, and the stale case has to travel on the same route, so one envelope for both is the honest shape.
2. **Real `lectio digest` emits `{"observations":[...]}`, not a bare array.** Found during the live check. The route now accepts a bare array *or* a single-key wrapper (`observations`/`items`/`lines`) and hands the panel the array either way; anything else is still a failure. New test `a wrapped observations array is unwrapped for the panel`.
3. **`peer_pr_lookback_days` is unused.** The `gh` command is exactly the one specified, which has no lookback flag, and filtering open PRs by age client-side would silently hide a peer's stalled PR — the opposite of what the panel is for. Left in config, unread; worth a follow-up decision.
4. **"Refresh on server start" lives in the `main` block, not `createServer`.** Otherwise every test that constructs a server would spawn real `gh` for any fixture peer file. Exposed as `server.hudRefreshPeers()`; the startup call is covered by the live check rather than a unit test.
5. Peers `stale` means "no successful refresh has written this snapshot in this process" — true on a cold start until the startup refresh lands, which is accurate: what's on screen is yesterday's file.

Not built, clean seam left as instructed: the `~/.claude` sessions panel (agents-0b4975) — `GET /api/dyn/sessions` is asserted to 404 today, and the UI comment names `renderPanel(id, env, build)` as the hook. No `skills/` paths touched. Bead deliberately left open.

HUD_ROOT is *pinned* to the tree containing the script rather than inherited, so the gate's subject cannot be redirected by ambient env. Port defaults to 4899, overridable via `HUD_SMOKE_PORT`.

## Output (run twice back to back, byte-identical apart from pid)

Idempotence confirmed: after two consecutive runs, port 4899 free, no `_hud/server.mjs` processes surviving, no `$TMPDIR/hud-smoke.*` left behind, `git status` clean.

## Spec coverage

All nine requested asserts plus the SPEC AMENDMENT are covered. Mapping: (1) ephemeral port + trap cleanup = 01/02/13; (2) tree floors = 03; (3) /api/md byte-match on a dynamically-picked real migrated note = 05; (4) board 200-or-503, never 500, server alive after = 06; (5) HTML at / = 07; (6) sessions 200 with count>=1 = 08; (7) POST 405 = 09; (8) graceful daemon-down + graft shape = 10; (9) `node --test` all green = 12.

Amendment specifics: (a) 08 additionally asserts `.root` is a real directory and that every group carries a non-empty project label and >=1 session, so ">=1 real session grouped under a project" is checked structurally, not just by count; (b) 09 probes POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, not POST alone, and re-checks the process afterwards; (c) 10 probes :7533 itself and, when the daemon is unreachable, requires top-level `.graft == "unavailable"` exactly — so a stubbed-out or vacuously-"live" graft would fail.

## Deviations from the literal spec — three, all deliberate

1. **The `graft` shape assert reads two levels, not one.** The spec said "the graft field is either an object or 'unavailable', nothing else". There are two `graft` fields with different types: the top-level whole-panel state is a *string enum* (`off` | `live` | `unavailable`, per `graftState()` in server.mjs:780) and can never be an object; the per-row `graft` is the one that is object-or-`"unavailable"` (`lectioGraft` in sessions.mjs:369-374). Asserting the literal wording against the top-level field would have failed on a correct server. So: top-level is checked against the three-value enum, and *every row* is checked as object-or-`"unavailable"`. Strictly stronger than the wording, and it matches the code's actual contract.

2. **Added assert 04, content parity, which the spec did not ask for.** Needed because the bead's own acceptance criterion ("verify smoke.sh is falsifiable by breaking one input, e.g. mv a playbook out, expect non-zero exit") does **not** hold against the spec as written: playbooks currently has 2 entries and the requested floor is `>=1`, total entries are 39 against a floor of `>=10`, so moving one playbook out passed all thirteen asserts. The floors have deliberate slack; slack means content can vanish and the gate still calls the tree healthy. Assert 04 adds an oracle for what *should* be present — every git-tracked `.md` under a section directory must still be served by /api/tree (root files, `_hud/`, and `raw/` contents excluded, matching SKIP_NAMES and the raw/-listing rule). Falls back to the migration manifest's `dest` list if the tree is not a git repo. Note the manifest alone would not have sufficed: it is a gitignored generated artifact, and `playbooks/jj-stacked-prs.md` was authored post-migration so it is not in the manifest at all.

3. **Added assert 11**, a check that the server logged no `request failed` line across the whole run. Cheap, and it catches a handled-but-real 500 that a status-code assert on one route would miss.

## Falsifiability — five distinct failure modes proven, all restored

Confirming the gate can fail; the orchestrator's own probes are still the gate on this.

- **`sessions.root` → missing dir** (the amendment's named probe): asserts 01-07 still pass (tree, content parity, md byte-match, board all green), then `FAIL /api/sessions reported root '/Users/…/.claude-does-not-exist-smoke-probe' which is not a directory`, exit 1. Config restored byte-identical (`git diff` clean).
- **`mv playbooks/jj-stacked-prs.md` out** (the acceptance criterion's named probe): `FAIL git-tracked notes name note(s) /api/tree no longer serves: playbooks/jj-stacked-prs.md`, exit 1 after 3 passes. **This probe passed vacuously before assert 04 existed** — see deviation 2. Restored.

title: Systematic graceful-degradation guard for Source implementations
description: Discovered via a real bug: LectioSource's construction path (tick-entry.ts calling lectioEnv(), which throws on missing env vars) violated the informal convention every other Source follows (construct with an empty-string env fallback, only ever throw inside fetch(), which runTick's per-source try/catch safely converts into a degradation entry). The convention is currently enforced by nothing but each Source author remembering it -- exactly the kind of thing a structural guard should catch instead. User specifically floated TS decorators as a possible mechanism (untested idea, not yet evaluated against simpler alternatives like a factory function wrapper or a lint rule). Needs real design thought before building: what's the actual guarantee to enforce (never throw synchronously in a constructor; or more specifically, never throw before fetch() is first called), what's the lightest-weight TS-native mechanism that enforces it (decorator vs factory vs lint rule vs a runtime wrapper class), and whether it's worth the complexity given there are currently only 4 Source implementations. Backlogged per user's explicit 'hold till linear, do the whole thing' instruction -- pick up alongside the other held items (pr-review-kit bundling, bot-detection-as-reusable-primitive, CI-rerun tool, fork-sync tool, worktree isolation/jj) once the linear-source build ships.
acceptance_criteria: a documented decision (not necessarily implemented) on whether/how to structurally enforce the never-throw-before-fetch convention across Source implementations

title: Adopt a shared type-driven-correctness review lens, generalized
description:
Adopts a review lens shared privately, built around the invariant-strength ranking — unrepresentable type > transaction boundary > machine-checked property > example test > prose — with three defect classes: parse-don't-validate demotions, examples where a universally-quantified property belongs, and hidden partial functions. The original author suggested generalizing it before wider use.

Generalized on three axes for this repo's agents/ registry:
1. Persona dropped. The original framed the discipline through a named practitioner while also instructing "you do not roleplay a persona; you apply a discipline" — the adoption completes that move and makes the discipline the whole identity.
2. De-repo-ified. Origin-codebase specifics became the generic patterns they instantiated — validate-then-forget, decorative wrappers, guarded-⊥ — plus a standing rule to read the target repo's own stated constraints and let them bound remedies.
3. De-language-ified where cheap. The ladder and defect classes are language-agnostic; the ⊥ hunting list is per-language (Rust, Go, TypeScript/Python) matching this ecosystem's split.

Kept in spirit: argued-vs-silent demotion as the load-bearing distinction, generator-theatre calibration, the invariant ledger output, and "no demotions worth acting on is a respectable verdict."

Frontmatter converted to this repo's Claude Code agent format, read-only tools per house convention for reviewers.

title: read_file returned empty for a missing fragment, silently blanking every consumer while the gate stayed green
description:
Found by an independent review of the include mechanism, and demonstrated against the migration landed in agents-6877ad rather than a hypothetical.

Deleting a _shared/ fragment and running `scripts/build.sh expand` removed the fragment's prose from all six consuming agents and `scripts/build.sh check` returned 0. In the reviewer's reproduction, "No findings worth acting on is a valid and respectable verdict" — the calibration guardrail — vanished from all six agents with a green gate.

Cause: read_file() in expand_file() looped `while ((getline line < p) > 0)` and returned "" for both EOF and the -1 error case, so a missing or unreadable path produced an empty replacement. check-includes could not catch it because `expand` had already written the empty version, leaving each file matching its own expansion — nothing to diff against.

The earlier mutation testing on agents-6877ad covered EDITS to a fragment and edits inside a block, both caught. It never covered DELETION of a fragment. A gate tested in one direction only.

Fixes:
1. read_file distinguishes getline's -1 from 0 and aborts with the file and fragment path named. An empty fragment also aborts, since a fragment that contributes nothing is a mistake rather than a valid state.
2. awk's exit status is captured in expand_file, so a failed read reports "include expansion aborted" rather than being misread as drift — the drift message sends the reader to `expand`, which is the command that caused the blanking.
3. read_file no longer swallows a leading blank line. The old accumulator treated out == "" as "nothing consumed yet", dropping a fragment's first line if it was empty — silent, permanent, and with no drift loop to reveal it.

Also lands the one trait extraction the review endorsed: the `**MCP dependency:** requires the rsry MCP server` line, byte-identical 6/6, into _shared/mcp-dependency-rsry.md. Verified that build.sh's body-level MCP rule survives the include (it greps the expanded file on disk, so the string is still present), and that deleting this particular fragment now fails via two independent paths.

Deliberately NOT extracted, per the review: the read-only sentence. Six phrasings, and an include would replace 1 line with 3 across 6 sites — +12 net lines to deduplicate a sentence whose payload is already carried by `disallowedTools: Write, Edit` in frontmatter and by each agent's `## Bead creation` section. Machinery exceeding payload. Unifying the wording in place remains an open editorial option, separate from extraction.</description>
<parameter name="issue_type">bug
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a _shared/ fragment makes `scripts/build.sh check-includes` exit non-zero, names the missing fragment, and leaves consuming agents unmodified; an empty fragment also fails; a fragment with a leading blank line round-trips stably; and `scripts/build.sh check` passes on the committed tree.

title: Skill allowed-tools reads as a restriction but grants — README column inverted, disallowed-tools rejected by lint
description:
Claude Code's allowed-tools PRE-APPROVES the listed tools for the invoking turn (clears on next user message) — it does not restrict; every tool stays callable. The restricting field is disallowed-tools. On the agent surface the semantics invert: tools:/disallowedTools: genuinely narrow.

Separately, disallowed-tools was absent from SKILL_ALLOWED_FIELDS, so adding the field that actually restricts failed lint as an unknown frontmatter key.

Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (allowed-tools / disallowed-tools semantics), https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills (Codex has no frontmatter equivalent; tool deps live in agents/openai.yaml).

title: hud: friendly deep-link URLs — path-as-slug routing for entries and sessions
description: User requirement: the URL must reflect what's on screen so views are shareable/bookmarkable; currently the path stays / while browsing. Scheme (fs-derived, no slug registry): /n/<repo-relative-entry-path> for content entries (trailing .md optional in the URL, restored on resolution), /s/<group>/<session-id> for sessions. Server: GET requests to /n/* and /s/* serve the app shell (ui/index.html) so deep links work on fresh load; traversal-guarded like /api/md; /api/*, /ui/*, / unchanged. UI: clicking an entry pushState's its /n/ URL; opening a deep link renders that entry (or a friendly not-found inside the shell); popstate handles back/forward; ⧉ copy-link affordance next to the open entry title. Watch-only unchanged (GET only). Export a pure route-resolution function for hermetic testing. Example: viewing projects/project-a/notes/2026-01-02-example.md ⇒ URL /n/projects/project-a/notes/2026-01-02-example.

comments.text:
Built and verified. Commit `05f91e7` — `feat(hud): deep-link URLs — path-as-slug routing`. Bead left open per instructions.

**What shipped**

`server.mjs` — exported `resolveRoute(target, opts)`. Pure without a root (reports the slug as written, touches no filesystem); given `{root}` it applies the one resolution rule — serve `<path>` if that file exists, else `<path>.md` — and realpath-contains the result. Returns `{kind:'entry'|'session'|'invalid'|null, path?, group?, id?, reason?}`.

Two deviations from the sketched contract, both deliberate:

1. Added `kind:'invalid'` alongside `'entry'|'session'|null`. A traversal attempt must produce 400 and a non-deep-link must fall through to the next route; one `null` cannot carry both. `reason` is the 400 body.
2. Routing matches the **raw** request target, not `url.pathname`. The WHATWG URL parser folds `..` away (and folds `%2e%2e` away too), so routing on the normalized pathname would silently rewrite a traversal attempt into whatever route it normalizes to rather than refusing it. Segments are decoded first, then judged: `..`/`.` rejected, and a decoded `/`, `\` or NUL rejected as a separator the split never saw. Then `resolveWithin` for realpath containment, so a symlink inside the root cannot tunnel out.

Unknown-but-well-formed deep links serve the shell (200) — the client owns "which entry", and a bookmark to a renamed note should land in a working app, not an error page. Non-GET on `/n|/s` falls into the existing method guard → 405. `/`, `/api/*`, `/ui/*` unchanged.

`ui/index.html` — clicking an entry `pushState`s its extensionless `/n/` URL; disclosing a session detail pushes `/s/<group>/<id>` (collapsing does not push, so history records views not toggles). `popstate` re-runs the same `applyLocation` a click uses. On first paint the location is applied once both addressable sources have answered (tree for `/n/`, sessions panel for `/s/`). An unresolvable link renders a friendly note above the tree with the tree still visible — not a doc view, not an error. One affordance added: a ⧉ button that copies `location.href`, in the doc bar and in each session detail. Nothing else changed; every route the page calls is still GET except the pre-existing peers refresh.

The page keeps its own copy of the path rules (four small pure functions) so it can read and write `location` without a round-trip. They sit between sentinel comments and the test extracts that block and diffs its answers against `resolveRoute`, so changing one and not the other fails the suite.

**Tests** — `test/routes.test.mjs`, hermetic (tmp fixture trees, port 0, generic names only: `project-a`, `example-playbook`). Seven cases, including the four required names verbatim, plus non-GET→405, `/s/<group>/<id>`→shell, `/`→shell, `/api/md` byte-exact against the on-disk file, and the client/server rule-parity case.

One harness note worth recording: neither `fetch` nor `curl` can drive a literal `/n/../../etc/passwd` to the server — both normalize dot segments (including the `%2e%2e` spelling, in undici's case) before the request goes out, so the server never sees the `/n/` prefix. The test opens a raw socket and writes the request target verbatim. `curl --path-as-is` works too; plain `curl` sends `/etc/passwd`, which is a safe 404.

```
node --test _hud/test/   →  52 passed, 0 failed  (45 pre-existing + 7 new)
smoke.sh (own port)      →  13/13 asserts held
```

**Live**, `HUD_PORT=4903`, run on a spare port so the long-running instance was never touched:

```
/n/<a real playbook slug>                 GET     200 text/html; charset=utf-8
/n/<same>.md                              GET     200 text/html; charset=utf-8
/n/x                                      POST    405 text/plain   "method not allowed"
/n/x                                      PUT     405 text/plain
/n/x                                      DELETE  405 text/plain
/s/g/i                                    POST    405 text/plain
/s/some-group/some-id                     GET     200 text/html
/n/inbox/no-such-note                     GET     200 text/html    (unknown → shell, not 500)
/api/tree                                 GET     200 application/json
/api/md?path=<a playbook>                 GET     200 text/plain
/                                         GET     200 text/html

curl --path-as-is /n/../../etc/passwd          400  "path escapes HUD_ROOT"
curl --path-as-is /n/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd  400  "path escapes HUD_ROOT"
curl (normalizing) /n/../../etc/passwd         404  (sent as /etc/passwd; never reaches /n)

diff <(deep link) <(/)                    → identical bytes
diff <(/api/md?path=…) <(file on disk)    → byte-exact
```

**Also touched**: added a Deep links paragraph to the app section of the HUD design/ops doc at the tree root. Left the self-hosted copy of the design doc alone — it describes intent rather than enumerating routes, and another session may be editing it.

**Not done**: no browser was available, so the client-side behaviors (pushState on click, popstate restore, the ⧉ copy) are verified by construction and by the rule-parity test, not by driving a page. That matches the falsifiability line on the bead, but it is the residual risk.

title: Retrofit severity rubric, inventory step and two-sided calibration into the six adversarial agents
description:
An anatomy scan across all agents found the set strong on domain and weak on mechanism: nearly every agent has an output format, almost none has a stated procedure, a severity rubric, or a calibration warning. The six adversarial reviewers had no severity axis at all — every finding was equally weighted, which makes a report nobody can triage.

Added three parts to each, structure identical and content domain-specific:

1. A severity rubric whose assignment is a TEST, not a feeling. Each agent gets BLOCKER/COMMENT/NOTE definitions in its own domain plus a one-line rule (e.g. enumeration: "a distinction an unauthorized caller can measure is a defect; one that exists in code but yields no attacker-usable bit is a comment; an argued, disclosed leak is a note").
2. An inventory-before-reporting step: name what was examined and cleared, not only what yielded findings, so coverage is checkable and a thorough pass is distinguishable from a lucky one.
3. A two-sided calibration warning naming both failure modes — the agent's specific zealotry mode and its specific credulity mode — closing with explicit permission that "no findings worth acting on" is a valid and respectable verdict.

Also replaces "lens" with house terminology throughout. agents/ never used the word; the six say "adversarial reviewer specializing in X" and skills/survey establishes "perspective" as the structural term (--perspectives, perspective:prod bead labels). "Lens" arrived with an externally-sourced agent and is now gone from agents/ entirely.</description>

acceptance_criteria: All six adversarial agents contain a `## Severity` section with a stated assignment rule, an inventory-before-reporting instruction, and a `## Calibration` section naming both failure modes; `grep -ri lens agents/` returns nothing.

title: work-board drops recurring same-titled events from the render — synthesized identity is not unique
description:
normalizeBoard synthesized artifactUri as kind:repo#number-or-title, falling back to the TITLE when no number exists. Calendar events carry neither repo nor number, so every occurrence of a recurring meeting got the identical key 'event:local#standup'.

render.ts joins on artifactUri as D3's key (lines 192 and 241). Duplicate keys are dropped from a D3 join rather than drawn over each other, so the second and later occurrences were never rendered. The board looked right — that is what made it hard to see.

dialLayout compounded it: it recovered an item's position with group.findIndex(e => e.artifactUri === item.artifactUri), which returns the FIRST match, so duplicates were also assigned one angle.

Proved before fixing: two same-titled standups both produced 'event:local#standup' and both landed at angle 81.

Fixed at the source — a number is left as the discriminator (appending activity there would break D3 object constancy and re-enter a PR on every update), and the occurrence time is added only where the title was all there was. dialLayout now records position during grouping, keyed by object identity, so it no longer depends on identities being unique.

Found while reading work-board as the reference pattern for hosting 0day's MCP server as a cloister bundle (0day-bd65c6).
acceptance_criteria: Two same-titled events with no repo/number get distinct artifactUris and distinct dial angles; a numbered artifact's identity does not change when its activity does. Verified by mutation.

title: Generate cloister [[gateway.skills]] digests from build.sh instead of hand-maintaining them
description:
cloister ADR-0061 declares skills in cluster.toml as [[gateway.skills]] entries with a sha256 digest, verified by resolvePlan before the run mints anything and refused on mismatch. That is the real enforcement boundary — skill frontmatter cannot express confinement at all.

The ergonomic cost is that every skill edit changes its digest and must be mirrored by hand into cloister's cluster.toml. Today only pr-board is pinned (sha256:8940e07e...) out of 39 skills, so the cost is mostly latent — it becomes real the moment more are declared.

build.sh already regenerates the README tables from the filesystem, so emitting the manifest block is the same shape of work, and it matches the argument taskfile-ci-parity already makes: one generated target, invoked by CI and hooks, rather than a second hand-maintained copy that drifts. Cross-repo: the generated block lands in ~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.toml.
acceptance_criteria: A build.sh target emits the [[gateway.skills]] block with current digests for every skill; regenerating after a skill edit produces the correct manifest diff with no hand-edited sha256

title: hud: entry viewer renders frontmatter as raw text — strip and show as metadata chips
description: User-reported rendering bug: opening an entry feeds the raw /api/md bytes (including the leading YAML frontmatter block) into marked, so the block renders as a run-together text line above the body. Fix in ui/index.html only: before rendering, detect a leading frontmatter block (same lenient rules as the server: starts with ---, ends at closing ---), strip it from the rendered body, and render a compact meta header instead — chips for type, status, date, tags, tickets (ticket chips become links via hud.config.json ticket_url_template when set), using the theme's badge styling. If the body's first heading equals the frontmatter title, don't duplicate; if there is no body heading, render the title as the view heading. Files with no frontmatter render exactly as before. Implement the strip/parse as ONE self-contained named function (e.g. function parseEntryMeta(md) { ... }) so it is extractable for testing. Add _hud/test/ui-meta.test.mjs: a hermetic node:test that reads ui/index.html, extracts that function's source by name, evaluates it, and asserts: strips a normal block; no-frontmatter input returned unchanged; malformed block (no closing ---) not stripped and not crashing; parsed keys (title/type/status/tags/tickets) come back correctly; body starting with a literal --- hr is not eaten.

comments.text:
Fixed. Changes confined to ui/index.html + new test/ui-meta.test.mjs, no server.mjs changes.

- Added `parseEntryMeta(md)` in ui/index.html: detects a leading frontmatter block (line 1 exactly `---`, closing `---` within a 400-line scan window, at least one `key: value` line inside), parses the same reduced YAML subset server.mjs's parseFrontmatter handles (scalars, quoted strings, `[a,b]` flow arrays, `key:` + `- item` block lists), and strips it from the body. Any of the three conditions failing leaves meta null and body byte-identical to the input — covers unclosed blocks and a document that legitimately opens with a markdown horizontal rule.
- Wired into openDoc(): body renders through marked as before; a `.meta-chips` row (reusing the existing `.badge` styling, no new hex colors) shows type/status/date/tags/tickets above it. Tickets link out via hud.config.json's `ticket_url_template` (fetched once via the existing /api/md route, which already serves arbitrary root-relative files as bytes — no new server route needed) unless the template points at an RFC 2606 reserved domain (example.com/.org/.net/.invalid), which is treated as unconfigured. If the body's first heading matches the frontmatter title there's no duplicate; if the body has no h1 at all, the frontmatter title is synthesized as the view's h1.
- New test/ui-meta.test.mjs extracts parseEntryMeta from the HTML by name (function-name to an `// parseEntryMeta:end` marker) and evaluates it via `Function`, then asserts the five named cases with real deepEqual/equal checks (not truthiness): strips normal frontmatter, no frontmatter unchanged, unclosed block not stripped, keys parsed, leading hr not eaten.

Verification:
- `node --test ~/hud/_hud/test/` → 58/58 green (52 prior + 6 new: the 5 named cases plus one harness-sanity check that the extracted source is a real function).
- Falsifiability probe: mutated the closing-fence regex (3 dashes → 4) in a scratch copy, reran just the new test file — it failed with real deepStrictEqual diffs (not a vacuous pass), confirming the tests check values. Reverted before committing.

No deviations from spec. Bead left open per instructions; not closing.

title: hud: loadout panel — skill/agent provenance + drift flags (watch-only)
description: User request (scoped down from full config introspection, which we deliberately rejected — no settings/permissions dumps, no predicting the harness's resolution rules). New GET /api/loadout: (1) inventory of ~/.claude/skills/* and ~/.claude/agents/* entries with provenance — for each: name, kind (file|symlink|dir), readlink chain fully resolved, whether the final target exists, and which known root it lives under (the HUD tree, a repo under the user's code roots, or standalone); (2) drift flags: broken symlink; skill dir present in a known repo's skills/ but absent from ~/.claude/skills (silently unloaded); name collision between ~/.claude and a repo-local .claude/skills; ~/.claude/projects/<slug> whose decoded path does not exist on disk (stale machine/user migration leftovers); (3) per-known-repo: does <repo>/.claude exist and which of skills/agents/settings files it carries (names only, never contents). Known repos derived from existing config/fs facts (e.g. dirs under the code roots already referenced by hud.config.json or the sessions slugs), not hardcoded. UI: LOADOUT panel in the right column — inventory rows with provenance glyph (link chain shown on hover/expand), drift flags surfaced at top in --yellow/--hot. Watch-only: GET only, names and paths only, no file contents. Tests: hermetic fixture ~/.claude-shaped tree + fixture repos: named cases "symlink provenance resolved", "broken symlink flagged", "unlinked repo skill flagged", "stale project slug flagged", "collision flagged", "loadout is get only", "no file contents in response" (assert response contains no settings values from fixture settings.json).

comments.text:
Shipped. Commit b67f2e9 in the HUD tree: `[agents-a660c5] feat(hud): loadout panel — provenance + drift flags`.

Server — `GET /api/loadout`, watch-only (one GET route, no POST arm, nothing cached, no snapshot written). Response: `{source, stale:false, generated_at, root, drift[], inventory:{skills[],agents[]}, repos[]}`. Per entry `{name, kind:file|symlink|dir, chain:[resolved readlink hops], targetExists, root:hud|repo:<n>|standalone|plugin}`; chain is empty for a non-link, so a linked skill and a locally-authored one are told apart by the chain rather than a flag. Root attribution takes the longest containing tree, so a repo nested under a discovered parent names itself.

Drift flags carry a server-side `severity` (hot|warn) so the panel does not re-derive the rule: broken-symlink and name-collision hot, unlinked-repo-skill and stale-project-slug warn. Collision is deliberately "two distinct definitions of one name" — a link that resolves *into* the repo is provenance, not collision; nothing here models which one the harness would pick.

Slug decoding is existence-guided depth-first, longest segment first (a directory whose own name contains a hyphen beats two directories), falling back to the naive full decode when nothing on disk breaks the tie — bounded by a step budget so a pathological slug costs bounded syscalls.

Config: `sources.loadout {claude_root}` defaulting to the documented root; absent means on (a local-filesystem source needs no endpoint), explicit `false` means 404 — the same panel-off contract sessions uses.

UI — LOADOUT panel in the right column: drift first, folded per flag kind so a long tail is one line until asked; then inventory rows with ⤳ for a link and an expandable chain; then the per-repo `.claude` presence and the names it carries. Existing badge/card styles and CSS vars only (added `.badge.hot` off `--hot`), zero external URLs, and the block contains no link-out, handler, navigation or fetch — the one interaction is a native `<details>` disclosure.

Tests — `test/loadout.test.mjs`, hermetic: one mkdtemp world holding a Claude-shaped root, two fixture repos, and a HUD tree, with generic fixture names throughout. The seven required cases plus a decoder unit case, the panel-wiring case, and both panel-off arms. All 58 prior tests stay green: **68 pass, 0 fail**.

Falsifiability — three mutation probes against the restored tree, each confirming the tests assert real values rather than truthiness: disabling the collision comparison fails only "collision flagged"; forcing the decoder to naive-only fails five cases including "stale project slug flagged"; making `carries.settings` return file contents instead of names fails "no file contents in response" *and* "symlink provenance resolved". Restored and re-run clean after each.

Live evidence (scratch port, background HUD untouched and still serving):
- GET 200, HEAD 200, POST/PUT/DELETE all 405.
- Real inventory: 33 skills, 26 agents, 14 discovered repos, roots spanning `repo:*`, `standalone` and `hud`.
- Real drift on this machine: 23 stale project slugs (the great majority decode to a home directory from a prior machine — they exist today, exactly as the bead predicted), 42 unlinked repo skills, 1 name-collision where a directory in the Claude root shadows a repo skill of the same name.
- Contents audit against the real settings file on disk: 21 distinct values and 30 distinct keys checked as substrings of the whole response body. The only matches are the JSON literals `true`/`false` and two coincidences inside genuine skill/agent *filenames*. No settings value, and no settings key, reaches the wire. The endpoint never opens a file — readdir, lstat, readlink, stat is its whole vocabulary.

One deviation from the acceptance criteria, and it is a real finding rather than a shortfall. The criterion expects the live default-root response to show the HUD's own skill with a chain resolving into the HUD tree. It does not, because that skill is **not linked into the Claude root at all** on this machine: the canonical copy lives in the HUD tree, the repo re-exports it as a relative symlink, and the last hop into the Claude root is missing — so the harness cannot load it. The panel surfaces this correctly as an unlinked-repo-skill flag, which is the drift the panel exists to catch. I did not create the missing link: it is outside this bead's file scope, it mutates the Claude root, and another thread owns that step.

The chain itself is verified live against the real trees, not only against fixtures: pointing the endpoint at a scratch Claude root containing that one link yields the two-hop chain (repo re-export, then the HUD tree) with `targetExists:true` and `root:"hud"`. Once the missing link lands, the default-root response will show that row unchanged.

Not closing — leaving that to the orchestrator.

IMMEDIATE PAYOFF: the panel's first real run flagged the hud skill itself as unlinked-repo-skill — it had never been linked into the global skills dir, so its slash-command discovery was silently broken; completed the per-skill symlink and the row moved from drift to inventory with the full two-hop chain (repo link -> HUD tree), and the skill then appeared live in a running session's inventory. Also surfaced ~23 stale project slugs from a prior machine, as predicted. KNOWN LIMITATION (accepted, on record): repo-scoped skills that deliberately live only in a repo's own .claude get flagged unlinked even though the harness loads them in-repo — flag severity split is a possible follow-up, not built (don't-over-build). title: hud: optional launchd persistence — configurable, fully reversible, self-documenting
description: User-approved persistence via launchd KeepAlive with two hard constraints: CONFIGURABLE and OBVIATED (optional sugar — the server must run identically without it; nothing may depend on the service existing). Build under ~/hud/_hud/service/: (1) install.sh — reads serve config from hud.config.json ("serve": {"host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 4870, "label": "local.hud"} — add this block with defaults; env HUD_PORT/HUD_ROOT still win), generates ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist from a template (RunAtLoad + KeepAlive, node + absolute server.mjs path resolved at install time, stdout/err -> _hud/generated/service.log which is already gitignored), loads via launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID, then health-checks with curl and prints status + the exact uninstall command. Idempotent: re-run replaces cleanly (bootout first if loaded). If the configured port is already held by a non-launchd process, say so and print the pid — do not silently kill. (2) uninstall.sh — bootout + remove plist + verify port released; leaves zero resident state. (3) Optional hostname: if serve.hostname is set, install.sh PRINTS the /etc/hosts line for the user to add themselves (never sudo inside the script) and notes the unprivileged-port-80 option on macOS. (4) README.md gains a short "Persistence (optional)" section stating the obviation guarantee: manual `node _hud/server.mjs` remains the canonical way to run; the service is a convenience with a one-command uninstall. Zero npm deps, zero PII, label/hostname generic defaults.

comments.text:
Shipped and verified live on the real machine. Commit `0bb3d3a` in the HUD tree (local only, not pushed): `_hud/service/{install.sh,uninstall.sh,plist.template}` + `serve` block in `hud.config.json` + "Persistence (optional)" README section. 463 insertions, 5 files. Paths below redacted as `<HOME>`.

## What was built

`install.sh` resolves every value as env > `hud.config.json` `serve` block > default: `HUD_ROOT` (default: script's `../..`), `HUD_PORT` (serve.port, else 4870), `HUD_LABEL` (serve.label, else `local.hud`), `HUD_HOST` (serve.host, else 127.0.0.1). Config is read via `node -e` JSON.parse rather than jq — node is already a hard requirement for the server, jq is not. Validates port range and constrains the label to `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` since it becomes both a launchd service name and a filename. Renders `plist.template` (committed with `@@PLACEHOLDER@@` tokens only) into `<HOME>/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist`, substituting in node rather than sed because user paths would let sed reinterpret `&` and the delimiter; a leftover-token check fails the install rather than shipping a broken plist. Loads via `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID` / boots out via `launchctl bootout` — modern interface, no legacy load/unload. Absolute node path resolved at install time (`command -v node`), and PATH seeded from where node/gh/digest-CLI actually live, because launchd supplies `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` and the panels shell out.

## Acceptance transcript

**Port refusal (run first, while a foreign process held the port):**
```
install.sh: port 4870 is already held by pid 52945:
52945 node <HOME>/hud/_hud/server.mjs
Refusing to touch a process this script did not start. Stop it yourself,
or pick another port (HUD_PORT=... or "serve".port in hud.config.json).
EXIT=1
```
The check compares the port holder against the pid launchd reports for our own label, so a re-install is never mistaken for a squatter.

**Install + health:** `launchctl print gui/501/local.hud` → exit 0, `state = running`, `properties = keepalive | runatload`, `program = /opt/homebrew/bin/node`. `curl /` → HTTP 200, `curl /api/tree` → HTTP 200.

**KeepAlive proof:** pid before kill `78602` → killed → new pid `78861` serving HTTP 200 within ~0.5s. `ASSERT PASS: pid changed`. Re-proved on the final persistent install: `82295` → `82359`, HTTP 200 after kill.

**Idempotence:** second `install.sh` → `replacing existing agent local.hud`, exit 0, `launchctl print` exit 0, HTTP 200, exactly one listener on the port and exactly one plist on disk. Existing agent is booted out *before* its plist is replaced, so a running process can never outlive the definition it started from.

**Uninstall:** exit 0 → `launchctl print` exit **113** (gone), plist `No such file or directory`, port free, `curl` → HTTP 000. Port verified from the plist being removed (via PlistBuddy) rather than from today's config, so what is checked is what was actually installed. Re-running with nothing installed → `nothing to remove`, exit 0.

**Obviation proof:** after uninstall, plain `node _hud/server.mjs` → HTTP 200, stdout normal. `grep -niE "launchd|launchctl|plist|LaunchAgents|service\.log|_hud/service"` over `server.mjs` → zero hits. `git show --stat HEAD` does not list `server.mjs` — it was not touched at all. `node --test _hud/test/` → **68/68 pass, 0 fail** (re-run after commit with the service live).

**Configurability proof:** `HUD_PORT=4871 HUD_LABEL=local.hud-altport install.sh` installed a second agent serving HTTP 200 on 4871 *alongside* the manual server on 4870; plist env confirmed `HUD_PORT => 4871`. `jq -e .serve.port` → 4870, `.serve.label` → `local.hud`; all five pre-existing config keys re-read intact.

**Hostname branch:** with `serve.hostname` set, install prints the `/etc/hosts` line for the user to run (`sudo tee` shown as text, never executed) plus the note that port 80 needs root the agent deliberately lacks. No `sudo` anywhere in either script.

**PII:** `grep -riE` for usernames/employer/`/Users/<user>` over the committed service files → clean. Committed template holds placeholders only; absolute paths exist solely in the generated plist under `<HOME>/Library`, which is not committed.

## Two real bugs the live run caught

1. **Symlinked root made the service flap silently.** `server.mjs` self-starts only when `argv[1]` matches the URL node loaded it from; node resolves symlinks, argv does not. Installing through a symlinked root (e.g. anything under `/tmp`, which is a symlink to `/private/tmp`) produced a process that exited 0 immediately and restarted forever under KeepAlive — `runs = 5`, `last exit code = 0`, empty log. Fixed in the installer with `pwd -P` (server unchanged), verified: root now resolves to the physical path and the service comes up healthy. The install-time health check is what surfaced this — it failed loudly with `launchctl print` + log tail instead of reporting success.
2. **The printed uninstall command named the wrong service under overrides.** `uninstall.sh` re-resolves root and label from env + config, so a bare `bash uninstall.sh` after an overridden install targeted the *config* label and cheerfully reported "nothing to remove" while the agent stayed loaded (reproduced: `local.hud-altport STILL LOADED`). Now the hint carries whichever of `HUD_ROOT=` / `HUD_LABEL=` was overridden; verified by running the printed command verbatim and confirming removal.

## Final state

Service **installed and running**, as requested: label `local.hud`, serving `http://127.0.0.1:4870/` (HTTP 200), KeepAlive active, log at `_hud/generated/service.log` (already gitignored). Uninstall is one command: `bash _hud/service/uninstall.sh` (`--purge-log` also removes the log). Not closing this bead.

comments.text:
Shipped + verified by building. Commit `26bb897` in the HUD tree (local, not pushed).

**Artifacts** (paths relative to `$HUD_ROOT`)
- `_hud/hud-schema.json` — mache v1 topology, 2 root nodes (`sections`, `panels`)
- `_hud/hud-index.mjs` — the record projector the schema reads
- `_hud/test/hud-index.test.mjs` — 6 hermetic tests (fixture tree, no real names)
- `projects/hud/notes/<dated>-mache-schema.md` — usage note; `index.md` + `log.md` updated

**Design deviation worth recording.** A schema alone cannot do this. mache's
tree-sitter selectors see one file at a time and only its *basename*
(`internal/ingest/engine_treesitter.go` passes `filepath.Base`), so no schema
over `*.md` can recover the directory chain that carries this tree's meaning.
The fix is mache's own documented two-stage idiom (`examples/audit-indexer.py`
+ `audit-schema.json`): flatten to `results(id, record)` rows, then name nodes
from record fields. Hence the indexer — it is load-bearing, not glue. It reuses
the existing tree/frontmatter parser rather than re-parsing, so the graph and
the HUD UI cannot disagree about what an entry says.

Two further mache facts that shaped the schema, both found empirically:
1. On the SQLite record path, **root node names are taken literally** and root
   selectors are ignored (`engine_sqlite.go:17-25` pre-creates roots from
   `nodeSchema.Name`). Templating starts at depth 1. So the two root nodes are
   structural category names and every *data*-derived name sits below them.
2. A JSON data source cannot be built to a `.db` at all — `--out` is only
   honoured on the `.db` and tree-sitter branches; a JSON source falls through
   to `mountNFS`, which wants sudo. A SQLite record index avoids the mount
   entirely.

**Build (exact commands + output)**
```
$ node _hud/hud-index.mjs
hud-index: <HUD_ROOT>/_hud/generated/hud-index.db
hud-index: 43 entries, 3 panels

$ mache "$(mktemp -d)" --schema _hud/hud-schema.json \
    --data _hud/generated/hud-index.db \
    --out  _hud/generated/hud.db --format sqlite
Loaded schema from _hud/hud-schema.json
Processed 46 records total.
Ingestion complete in 9.472083ms
Wrote _hud/generated/hud.db (format: sqlite)
```
(the `mktemp -d` positional is never mounted — mache's root command parses a
mountpoint even when `--out` means it won't use one)

**Materialized shape**
```
sections/<section>/<group>/<subgroup>/<slug>/{title,path,type,status,date,tags,tickets,repos,gh}
panels/<source>/{kind,target}
```
688 nodes, 181 ref edges over 64 distinct tokens.

**Top-level / section nodes match the real content dirs.** Top-level graph
nodes are `sections`, `panels`, `_schema.json` (mache's own). The section-level
nodes are exactly the three content directories holding ≥1 non-dotfile —
verified by diffing against a `find`-per-directory count. The two sections
holding only `.gitkeep` materialize nothing (no entries → no node), and the
machinery dir and `.git` are excluded.

**An entry resolves with frontmatter-derived files.** Queried one dated project
note: `title`, `path`, `type`, `status`, `date` carry scalars; `tags` and
`tickets` carry newline-joined lists; `repos`/`gh` are empty for a non-peer
entry. Each list value is also its own child node carrying a ref.

**Ref-edge across entries proven.** One `tag:` token resolves to three
different entries — a playbook in one section plus two dated notes in a project
group in another section — i.e. a single token linking three nodes whose only
relationship is the shared frontmatter value. Ticket tokens behave the same
(the largest links six entries). Token families: `tag:`, `ticket:`, `repo:`,
`type:`, `status:`, `gh:`, `panel-kind:`. Zero `<no value>` tokens or node ids
(asserted by query; the first build had 11 and the `{{if}}` guards fixed it).

**Zero hardcoded work names.** Grepped the schema for every on-disk section,
project, ticket prefix and tag — no hits. A test asserts the same against two
canary fixture names and asserts the names it *does* carry are templates.

**diagram-gen-spec handoff verified.** `mache serve <built .db> --schema
<schema> --path $HUD_ROOT` → `list_directory` walks the section tree and
`get_diagram` returns a mermaid graph clustered by shared tags/tickets/status
rather than by directory. Two sharp edges documented in the note: `--path` is
required (without it every tool call fails "workspace root unavailable"), and
`serve` must be pointed at the *built* graph, not the record index (it expects
`nodes` to exist and fails writing virtuals otherwise).

**Tests**: `node --test _hud/test/` → 79 passed, 0 failed (6 new).

Not closing per instructions.

title: sync-branch: mechanize the fetch/stash/checkout-main/pull/checkout-back/rebase git recipe, pause only at conflicts
description: User's exact described workflow, currently fully manual: 'Sync fork (don't lose current branch state) -> git fetch -> stash -> checkout main -> pull -> checkout branch -> rebase -> resolve conflicts -> push -> tell Claude it's ok I did it'. Every step except 'resolve conflicts' is pure mechanism -- the user currently does the WHOLE thing by hand and only tells Claude once it's done, rather than delegating the mechanical bookend steps and only handling (or being handed) the judgment part. Design: a script that runs fetch/stash/checkout-main/pull/checkout-branch/rebase automatically, and EITHER pauses cleanly with clear state if rebase hits a conflict (leaving the repo in a normal mid-rebase state the user or Claude can resolve), or completes straight through (stash-pop, done) if no conflicts. Should NOT auto-push -- that's likely still a separate, explicit step given push is broadly considered higher-stakes than a local rebase.
acceptance_criteria: a new ~/.local/bin script that mechanizes fetch->stash->checkout main->pull->checkout branch->rebase, stopping cleanly at a real conflict rather than needing the whole recipe done by hand

title: hud: TOML config (hud.toml) with useful serve defaults incl. hostname
description: User request: hand-editable simple TOML config + useful naming defaults. (1) Add a TOML-subset parser to the server (node stdlib has none; follow the codebase idiom of the lenient frontmatter parser): [section] tables, dotted keys ok to skip, key = "string" | integer | true/false, # comments, whitespace tolerant; malformed line -> skipped with a warn list, never a crash. (2) New canonical config ~/hud/hud.toml migrated from hud.config.json values, plus defaults: [serve] host=127.0.0.1, port=4870, label="local.hud", hostname="hud.internal" (used only for printed /etc/hosts guidance; .internal is ICANN-reserved private-use, .local collides with mDNS). (3) Server loads hud.toml if present, else falls back to hud.config.json (peers who copied earlier keep working); repo ships hud.toml only — delete hud.config.json after migrating. (4) Update every consumer: _hud/service/install.sh (read via node -e with the SAME parser, not jq), _hud/hud-index.mjs (panels source), smoke.sh if it reads config, README + HUD.md + the system-map note mentions. (5) Tests: hermetic config.test.mjs — named cases "toml sections and scalars parse", "comments and blank lines ignored", "malformed line skipped with warning not crash", "json fallback used when toml absent", "toml wins when both exist". All existing suites stay green; mache rebuild (node _hud/hud-index.mjs) still succeeds. Zero npm deps, zero PII.

comments.text:
Implemented and verified. Committed locally as ac25c2e (17 files, +575/-81); not pushed.

**(1) Parser.** `parseToml(text) -> {data, warns}` in server.mjs, placed directly after `parseFrontmatter` as its sibling and documented as the same bargain (no stdlib TOML, no dependency, lenient). Subset: `[table]` and `[dotted.table]` headers, `key = "string"` (double-quoted with escapes, single-quoted literal), integers, `true`/`false`, whole-line `#` comments, trailing `# comment` after a value *or* a header, whitespace tolerant. Outside the subset -> line skipped, described in `warns`, never thrown: dotted bare keys, arrays, inline tables, floats, dates, `[[array of tables]]`, unterminated strings, empty values.

Warn behavior verified live rather than only in test: a tmp root with `[serve]/port = 4931/broken line here/label = "tmp.hud"` printed exactly `hud: hud.toml: line 3: not a [table] header or a key = value line`, then started and served — and `label` (the line *after* the damage) still parsed. Warns print once from the main block only; `loadConfig` is called per request and deliberately logs nothing, so a bad line does not reprint on every panel refresh.

**(2) hud.toml.** Values migrated verbatim and machine-checked for parity against the old JSON before deletion (board url, digest cmd, sessions root+lectio, peer_pr_lookback_days, ticket_url_template all byte-identical; only addition is `[serve] hostname`). `[serve]` = host 127.0.0.1, port 4870, label local.hud, hostname "hud.internal". Heavily commented since it is now the hand-edited file, including a comment explaining why the two top-level keys sit above the first table — real TOML assigns every key after a `[table]` header to that table, which I hit as an actual bug on the first draft (the two keys silently became `serve.*`) and fixed by layout rather than by bending the parser.

**(3) Fallback + delete, in that order.** Landed the code with the JSON fallback intact and green *first* (84 pass), then migrated, then deleted `hud.config.json` via `git rm` (tracked and unmodified, so recoverable from history). `loadConfigDetail` returns `{data, warns, file}`; TOML wins whenever a readable hud.toml exists, including present-but-empty — "I emptied the config" is an answer, not an absence, and falling back there would override it. Not merged with the JSON: a key only the JSON carries stays unread, otherwise deleting a source from hud.toml would fail to switch its panel off.

**(4) Consumers.** install.sh + uninstall.sh read `[serve]` by importing the server's own `loadConfig` — one parser, no shell reimplementation, no jq (gate `grep -q '\bjq\b' install.sh` clean). Arguments travel in the environment, not argv: server.mjs self-starts when `argv[1]` names it, so passing its path would have left `cfg_get` binding the port it was called to inspect. uninstall.sh additionally swallows failure and falls through to the default label, because removal has to work on a broken tree. hud-index.mjs needed no code change (already imports loadConfig); its doc comment updated. smoke.sh preflight now requires hud.toml. UI: replaced the `/api/md?path=hud.config.json` raw-bytes fetch with a new `GET /api/config` returning the parsed config — a browser has no TOML reader and must not grow a second copy of this one. Exposes nothing new (/api/md already served the file verbatim); POST returns 405 like every other route here. Three user-facing "not configured in ..." error strings now name hud.toml; two existing tests asserting the old string were updated.

**(5) Tests.** New hermetic `_hud/test/config.test.mjs` with the five named cases, tmp roots only, no network, no real tree: "toml sections and scalars parse" (incl. typed scalars — port is a number, `loadout = false` is a boolean — and re-entering an existing table), "comments and blank lines ignored" (incl. a `#` inside quotes surviving as part of a URL), "malformed line skipped with warning not crash" (9 malformed shapes, asserts the good keys around the damage survive, that nothing refused leaked in under any name, that keys after an unusable header do not fall into the preceding table, and that empty/BOM/`[`/`[a.]`/bare-quote inputs do not throw), "json fallback used when toml absent" (plus no-config and unparseable-JSON), "toml wins when both exist" (plus present-but-empty, plus the /api/config route and its 405).

**Evidence.** `node --test _hud/test/` 84 passed / 0 failed (79 baseline + 5 new), run again after every subsequent edit. `bash _hud/smoke.sh` 13/13 against the real tree. `node _hud/hud-index.mjs` succeeds: 43 entries, 3 panels — same as before the migration, and hud-index's own fixture was switched to TOML so the index test exercises the canonical path non-vacuously (asserts 2 panels out of a hud.toml fixture). `bash -n` clean on all three shell scripts; server.mjs imports clean.

**Live service.** Reinstalled twice — once after the config migration, once more after the final comment edits so the running process is the committed code. `launchctl print gui/501/local.hud`: state = running, pid 7701, last exit code = (never exited). Routes on :4870 all 200: `/`, `/api/tree`, `/api/config`, `/api/sessions` (11 sessions, 3 groups), `/api/loadout`, `/api/dyn/board`. service.log clean — no config warnings, because hud.toml parses with zero warns. install.sh printed the hostname guidance block, which only fires when `cfg_get hostname` returns non-empty: proof the TOML parser is what fed the installer. Left running and healthy.

**Deviations, all deliberate.** (a) The bead said "update every consumer" — the UI needed a new `/api/config` route rather than an in-place edit, because client-side TOML parsing would duplicate the parser in the browser; chose the route as the smallest correct change and documented the reasoning at the route and at the call site. (b) Added `loadConfigDetail` alongside `loadConfig` rather than changing the existing signature: 8 call sites want only the values, and only the startup path wants the warns. (c) Left `hud.config.json` fixtures in dynamic/sessions-wire/static/loadout tests — they now exercise the fallback path, which is free coverage of the thing most likely to rot. (d) Did not rewrite the dated historical notes (`log.md`'s 2026-09-10 scaffold line, the 2026-09-10 design doc) that mention the old filename; those record what was true then, and editing them would falsify the record. Appended a migration entry to log.md instead, which is what that file is for. Zero npm deps, zero PII (grep clean), every URL loopback or RFC 2606 reserved. Bead left open per instruction.
